mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: an unported branch of this command: dothrow.c reached throwing an artifact

summary: The first mismatch is the blanket artifact refusal in js/dothrow.js throw_obj(). Upstream throw_obj() restricts only Mjollnir, so Grimtooth proceeds through the ordinary throw path. The saved C step ends with the orc picking up the landed dagger; it does not exercise a thrown hit or artifact_hit().

source.branch: After a successful item selection and northward direction, the selected singleton is the non-Mjollnir artifact Grimtooth. Upstream throw_obj() permits this object; only Mjollnir must be wielded and meet its strength requirement. The missile proceeds to throwit(), lands, and the orc later picks it up.
callers: dothrow.c:dothrow() (352-375) calls throw_obj() after #throw selects an object; cmd.c:1901-1902 dispatches the "throw" row to dothrow(). The recorded key t follows js/cmd.js:5970-5986 -> dothrow() -> throw_obj().
dothrow.c:dofire() (469-585) also calls throw_obj() for its selected quivered/fireassist object; js/dothrow.js:dofire() is the matching production caller.
dependencies: dothrow.c:throwit() receives the selected missile after inventory removal; it uses zap.c:bhit() with THROWN_WEAPON and null callbacks.
dothrow.c:throwit() reaches dothrow.c:breaktest() on the hard landing; breaktest() calls zap.c:obj_resists(), matching the first recorded RNG draw at step 48.
do.c:flooreffects() handles the landing before dothrow.c:throwit() places the dagger.
monmove.c:postmov() reaches mon.c:mpickstuff() after the monster moves onto the floor object; this produces the recorded orc pickup message.

apply.c:snuff_candle() is a later discarded-result call in throwit(); js/dothrow.js records note_unported("apply.c snuff_candle"). It has no effect here because Grimtooth is not a lit candle or candelabrum.

The whole throw_obj() source unit also contains separate throw_obj() placeholder branches for instapetrify(), weldmsg(), dry_a_towel(), is_quest_artifact(), and unsplitobj(); their predicates are not reached by this singleton-dagger case.

evidence: Saved handoff .cache/v16-investigations/7.json points to challenges/evaluations/20261001125731-v16.json (evaluation commit 452fff60d85992524c72a8282fbae13a5e32a906): 1 remaining screen, 49 recorded steps, and a stop at zero-based step 48 with "unsupported hero command: an unported branch of this command: dothrow.c reached throwing an artifact".

At the examined main commit, nethack-c/upstream/src/dothrow.c:122-131 blocks an artifact only when it is ART_MJOLLNIR (not wielded or too heavy); other artifacts continue. js/dothrow.js:2075-2078 instead refuses every obj.oartifact, which is the exact first-stop owner. The actionable scope is the whole C throw_obj() function, dothrow.c:87-292, including its direction handling, item restrictions, multishot and inventory transitions, throwit() handoff, and unsplit cleanup.

The production caller chain is nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:1901-1902 extcmdlist["throw"] -> dothrow.c:dothrow():352-375 -> throw_obj(); js/cmd.js:5970-5986 dispatches the recorded throw command through dothrow(). dothrow.c:dofire():469-585 is the other C caller and must remain wired to the same whole-function port.

The C recording challenges/cases/v16/rogue-throws-grimtooth-at-hostile-orc.session.json, segment 0 step 48, shows "The orc picks up a poisoned orcish dagger named Grimtooth." Its first RNG call is obj_resists(), the hard-landing check reached from throwit()->breaktest(); the remaining logged calls include monster movement/move timing and ordinary end-of-turn processing. There is no ordinary thrown-hit rnd(20) draw, so this case does not establish the thitmonst()/hmon()/artifact_hit() branch. The observed downstream behavior is landing and monster pickup.

Later source gaps remain distinct from the first refusal. js/dothrow.js:2250-2259 still refuses the C throw_obj() unsplitobj() cleanup arm, which this single-item path skips after setting obj to null. js/dothrow.js:2811 records the skipped discarded-result apply.c:snuff_candle() call; upstream apply.c:1472-1491 changes state only for a lit candle or candelabrum, so it is inert for Grimtooth. The recorder patch README describes only deterministic runtime, stable sorting, RNG logging, and terminal capture; no patch changes dothrow.c or artifact gameplay.
